name: The Komlos-Sulyok-Szemeredi bound: every finite set of reals has a Sidon subset of size c sqrt n
description:
Call a set of reals a *Sidon set* when all its pairwise sums are distinct: if $a + b = c + d$ with all four in the set, then $\{a,b\} = \{c,d\}$.

The goal is to show that for some absolute constant $c > 0$, every finite set $X$ of positive reals contains a Sidon subset $S$ with $|S| \ge c\sqrt{|X|}$.

This is the lower bound half of [Erdos problem 530](https://www.erdosproblems.com/530), which Riddell posed and which asks for the order of the largest guaranteed Sidon subset. That problem is open: it asks whether the guarantee is asymptotically $N^{1/2}$, and the constant is not known. Komlos, Sulyok, and Szemeredi, *Linear problems in combinatorial number theory*, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 26 (1975) 113-121, settled the order as a case of a general theorem about linear equations. Erdos had previously observed the cube-root lower bound and the matching $(1+o(1))N^{1/2}$ upper bound from $A = \{1, \dots, N\}$. A second and much shorter proof is in Bailleul and Riblet, [arXiv:2605.03181](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03181).

## The exponent is the whole problem

A one-paragraph argument gives $|S| \ge c|X|^{1/3}$: take a Sidon subset $S$ of maximum size, and note that every $x$ outside it satisfies $x = c + d - b$ or $x = (c+d)/2$ for elements of $S$, so $|X| \le 3|S|^3$.

That cube root is not a weak first attempt, it is the ceiling for any argument that only counts. An arithmetic progression of length $n$ has additive energy of order $n^3$, so a probabilistic argument cannot see the difference between it and a generic set. Getting from $1/3$ to $1/2$ requires using the structure of the set, and that is what both published proofs do.

## The idea both proofs share

Compress, then pigeonhole against a known Sidon set.

An arbitrary finite set of reals lacks any arithmetic to work with, so first move it into $\mathbb{Z}$: a finite set spans a finite dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space, and a generic rational functional separates its points while preserving every relation $a + b = c + d$. Then squeeze the resulting integers into an interval of length comparable to their number, keeping a constant fraction of them and keeping the property that a Sidon subset of the image lifts to one of the original. Finally intersect with a translate of the Erdos-Turan Sidon set, which has about $\sqrt{N}$ elements inside $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. A set of size $\Theta(n)$ inside $[1,n]$ meets some translate of a Sidon set of size $\sqrt{n}$ in order $\sqrt{n}$ points, and that intersection is Sidon.

The two proofs differ only in the compression step, and the mission contains both.

## The two routes

The 1975 route compresses in four lemmas driven by a remainder map: choose a modulus $q$ dividing no difference, dilate so that the remainders are small, and observe that a small remainder map preserves $a + b = c + d$. Finding the modulus needs a prime counting bound.

The 2026 route replaces all four with one averaging lemma over a real rotation parameter $\theta$, keeping the elements whose fractional part of $am\theta$ is below $1/2$, where no carry occurs. No prime counting appears anywhere.

## Notes on the formalization

Every item is stated in Mathlib primitives alone, so definition items are unnecessary here. The Sidon condition, the Erdos-Turan construction, and the reduction relation of the 1975 route are all written out at each use.

The published 2026 proof finishes with Singer's 1938 covering of $\mathbb{Z}/(q^2+q+1)\mathbb{Z}$ by $q+1$ Sidon sets. Perfect difference sets are missing from Mathlib, so the mission uses averaging over translates instead. It does the same job at the same order and gives a worse constant, which is fine because the goal asserts only that some $c > 0$ exists.

Two lemmas of the 1975 paper are deliberately absent. A local formalization of Lemma 2 and Lemma 6 turned out to be false as stated, machine-checked in both cases, so neither is offered here as a milestone. Those are errors in that rendering rather than in the paper, and the 2026 route reaches the goal without either. Lemma 1' is absent for the same practical reason: the 2026 route does not need it.
note: item_order lists theorem names, not server item ids. Neither assembly node of the source bench is an item: both prove the goal statement itself, so uploading them would be three items carrying one statement. The two routes are described in the mission description instead.
